paraphrase: The soul (haṃs) that receives the true Name from the guru of Kabīr's line, with the pān-parvānā, is let pass by Kāl's messengers at death and returns to Satlok, never to be reborn.

location.ref: Anurāg Sāgar, Kabīr's descents in the four ages

paraphrase: Kabīr (the Sat Puruṣ's messenger) came in each age to free souls from Kāl: as Sat Sukṛt in the Satya age, Munīndra in the Tretā, Karuṇāmay in the Dvāpara and Kabīr in the Kali; Kāl obtained the promise that only those who receive the true Name would be freed.

location.ref: Anurāg Sāgar, Kāl Nirañjan's austerities and the three worlds

paraphrase: Nirañjan performed austerities and won from the Sat Puruṣ the three worlds and the goddess Ādyā (Aṣṭāṅgī); he swallowed her, was cast out of Satlok, and with her begot Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheś; he became Kāl, who devours beings and hides the true Lord, and made souls forget Satlok.

location.ref: Anurāg Sāgar, creation section (the Sat Puruṣ and his sixteen sons)

paraphrase: In the beginning the Sat Puruṣ alone was; by his word he brought forth sixteen sons (islands of light), among them Kūrma and Nirañjan; all dwelt in Satlok in bliss.
